text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- KLM/Royal Dutch Airlines books three times higher Q1 operational profit due to fuller aircraft. (p1)
- Unexpectedly low penicillin prices force Gist-Brocades to downgrade its profits forecast. (p1)
- Record throughput in the port of Rotterdam is argument for the port's extension onto the second Maasvlakte. (p1)
- Continuing rise of the dollar pushes up interest rates of Dutch capital markets. (p1)
- Publisher Wolters Kluwer adjusts its profits forecast upwards. (p3)
VOLKSKRANT
- Swine fever is spreading north into the province of Overijssel. (p1)
- There is room for a six percent rise in wage costs, according to MKB, the association of small and medium-sized businesses. (p1)
- Future of KLM's subsidiary Martinair remains uncertain. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Jobs in small and medium-sized business sector are growing explosively. (p7)
- Builder HBG's subsidiary Wayss & Freytag sees recovery of Germany's building sector. (p21)
- Economic confidence in the Netherlands is the highest in Europe, according to European Commission's economic barometer.
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Price range of shares in Ispat, the Indian steel concern which is to be listed in New York and Amsterdam tomorrow, is raised to $26-27. (p12)
TROUW
- Sugar producer Cosun takes majority stake in Slovenian sugar plant. (p7)
